## Phase 7: User Story 5 - Missing Metric Scores (Priority: P2)

**Goal**: Thresholds for metrics with no score always fail (don't pass or crash)

**Independent Test**: Run evaluation without references (exact_match has no score) with threshold on exact_match; verify threshold fails

### Implementation for User Story 5

- [ ] T028 Verify null score handling in evaluateThresholds in packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js
  - Condition: if (score === null || score === undefined) → passed = false
  - No special case, just comparison `>= null` yields false
- [ ] T029 Add tests for null/undefined scores in packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js
  - Test: Metric with score: null → threshold fails (passed: false)
  - Test: Metric with score: undefined → threshold fails (passed: false)
  - Test: Report shows score: null in thresholds array
- [ ] T030 Add tests for missing data in packages/frai-cli/src/index.test.ts
  - Test: `frai eval --outputs data.json --threshold exact_match=0.9` (no references)
  - Expected: exit 1 (threshold fails because exact_match has no score)
  - Expected: report shows exact_match threshold with score: null, passed: false
- [ ] T031 Add Markdown formatting test for null scores in packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.test.js
  - Test: Threshold with null score shows as "no score available" in Markdown
  - Test: Overall status is FAIL when any threshold has null score

**Checkpoint**: Null/undefined scores correctly fail thresholds; behavior is safe and predictable

  - Scenario 1: Threshold passes → exit 0 ✓

  - TypeScript definitions for threshold-related functions

  - Existing SDK code calling generateReport without thresholds param works unchanged
  - Report format unchanged when thresholds not specified

  - Document validateThresholds, evaluateThresholds, formatThresholdError
  - Document generateReport threshold parameter
  - Include examples of usage

  - SDK: Programmatically validate same data, verify results match

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies - verify existing packages
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup - provides core functions for all stories
- **User Story 1 (Phase 3, P1)**: Depends on Foundational - CLI feature
- **User Story 2 (Phase 4, P1)**: Depends on Foundational - SDK feature
- **User Story 3 (Phase 5, P2)**: Depends on US1 and US2 - report formatting
- **User Story 4 (Phase 6, P2)**: Depends on Foundational - error handling
- **User Story 5 (Phase 7, P2)**: Depends on Foundational - null handling
- **Polish (Phase 8)**: Depends on all user stories - comprehensive testing

### User Story Dependencies

- **US1 (CLI Gate)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - No dependencies on other stories
- **US2 (SDK Validation)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - Independent of CLI
- **US3 (Report Writing)**: Depends on US1 AND US2 both being mostly complete (report format)
- **US4 (Validation Errors)**: Depends on Foundational - error messages
- **US5 (Null Scores)**: Depends on Foundational - null handling

### Within Each Phase

- Tests → Implementation (each story's tests before implementation)
- Models → Services → Endpoints → Integration
- Validation before main logic

### Parallel Opportunities

- All Phase 2 tasks marked [P]: validation functions, helper functions can run in parallel
- US1 CLI tasks and US2 SDK tasks can run in parallel (both depend only on Phase 2)
- Within Phase 3 (US1): argument parsing and validation can be developed in parallel, then integrated
- Within Phase 4 (US2): generateReport modification and tests can run in parallel
- Within Phase 5 (US3): JSON and Markdown reporters can be modified in parallel
- Phase 2 must complete before US1/US2 start, but US1/US2 can proceed in parallel

Both run in parallel; only dependency is Phase 2 completion.

### MVP First (User Story 1 + 2)

1. Complete Phase 1: Setup

3. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1 (CLI)

5. **STOP and VALIDATE**: Run quickstart scenarios 1-3, 9-10
6. Deploy if ready

### Incremental Delivery

1. Phase 1 + Phase 2 → Foundation ready

# Tasks: Eval Threshold Validation

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/001-eval-thresholds/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story to enable independent implementation and testing of each story.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependencies on incomplete tasks)
- **[Story]**: Which user story this task belongs to (e.g., US1, US2, US3, US4, US5)
- Include exact file paths in descriptions

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies - verify existing packages
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup - provides core functions for all stories
- **User Story 1 (Phase 3, P1)**: Depends on Foundational - CLI feature
- **User Story 2 (Phase 4, P1)**: Depends on Foundational - SDK feature
- **User Story 3 (Phase 5, P2)**: Depends on US1 and US2 - report formatting
- **User Story 4 (Phase 6, P2)**: Depends on Foundational - error handling
- **User Story 5 (Phase 7, P2)**: Depends on Foundational - null handling
- **Polish (Phase 8)**: Depends on all user stories - comprehensive testing

### User Story Dependencies

- **US1 (CLI Gate)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - No dependencies on other stories
- **US2 (SDK Validation)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - Independent of CLI
- **US3 (Report Writing)**: Depends on US1 AND US2 both being mostly complete (report format)
- **US4 (Validation Errors)**: Depends on Foundational - error messages
- **US5 (Null Scores)**: Depends on Foundational - null handling

### Within Each Phase

- Tests → Implementation (each story's tests before implementation)
- Models → Services → Endpoints → Integration
- Validation before main logic

### Parallel Opportunities

- All Phase 2 tasks marked [P]: validation functions, helper functions can run in parallel
- US1 CLI tasks and US2 SDK tasks can run in parallel (both depend only on Phase 2)
- Within Phase 3 (US1): argument parsing and validation can be developed in parallel, then integrated
- Within Phase 4 (US2): generateReport modification and tests can run in parallel
- Within Phase 5 (US3): JSON and Markdown reporters can be modified in parallel
- Phase 2 must complete before US1/US2 start, but US1/US2 can proceed in parallel

  - If thresholds NOT provided: skip (backwards compatible, no new fields)
- [x] T015 Add threshold evaluation logic in packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js (generateReport)
  - Call evaluateThresholds(thresholds, evaluations)
  - Add `passed: boolean` field (true if all thresholds passed)
  - Add `thresholds: array` field with threshold results
  - Only add these fields if thresholds parameter was provided
- [x] T016 Add SDK tests in packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js
  - Test: generateReport with thresholds → includes passed and thresholds fields
  - Test: All thresholds pass → passed: true
  - Test: Any threshold fails → passed: false
  - Test: Metric with null score → threshold fails (passed: false)
  - Test: Unknown metric in thresholds → throws Error with valid metric IDs listed
  - Test: generateReport without thresholds → no new fields (backwards compat)
- [x] T017 Add integration test for SDK usage in packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js
  - Create mock evaluations with known scores
  - Call generateReport with custom thresholds
  - Verify report structure and passed status match expectations

---

## Phase 5: User Story 3 - Partial Failures with Complete Reporting (Priority: P2)

**Goal**: Reports are written even when thresholds fail, so users see diagnostic data

**Independent Test**: Run evaluation with failing threshold; verify report file is created with full metric details

### Implementation for User Story 3

- [x] T018 [P] Modify JSON report output in packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js (toJson)
  - Ensure `passed` and `thresholds` fields are included in JSON output when present in report
  - Format: standard JSON with proper indentation (already done by JSON.stringify)
- [x] T019 [P] Modify Markdown report output in packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js (toMarkdown)
  - Add "## Thresholds" section after "## Metrics" section (when thresholds present)
  - Format: list each threshold with `- **{metric}** (min: {min}): {PASS/FAIL} (score: {score})`
  - Show "no score available" instead of null
  - Add "**Overall**: PASS/FAIL" line at end of section
- [x] T020 Add tests for JSON report with thresholds in packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.test.js
  - Test: toJson includes passed and thresholds fields
  - Test: Valid JSON output (can be parsed)
- [x] T021 Add tests for Markdown report with thresholds in packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.test.js
  - Test: toMarkdown includes "## Thresholds" section
  - Test: Each threshold shows correct PASS/FAIL status
  - Test: Shows "no score available" for null scores
  - Test: Overall PASS/FAIL matches report.passed
- [x] T022 Add CLI integration test for reporting in packages/frai-cli/src/index.test.ts
  - Test: Report written to file even when threshold fails (exit 1)
  - Test: Report contains all metrics details + thresholds section
  - Test: Report file is valid JSON/Markdown

## Phase 6: User Story 4 - Validation Error Detection (Priority: P2)

## Phase 8: Polish & Cross-Cutting Concerns

**Purpose**: Final improvements and comprehensive validation

- [ ] T032 [P] Update frai-core package exports in packages/frai-core/src/index.js
  - Ensure Eval module still properly exports all public functions
  - Verify no breaking changes to existing exports

  - Ensure EvalOptions interface includes thresholds if needed
  - Update type definitions for threshold parameter

  - Command: `pnpm test` in each package
  - Verify all new tests pass
  - Verify no regressions in existing tests

  - Command: `pnpm build` in each package
  - Verify no TypeScript/linting errors
  - Verify built output is correct

  - Scenario 1: Threshold passes → exit 0 ✓
  - Scenario 2: Threshold fails → exit 1 ✓
  - Scenario 3: Multiple thresholds → correct exit ✓
  - Scenario 4: Malformed threshold → exit 2 ✓
  - Scenario 5: Invalid range → exit 2 ✓
  - Scenario 6: Unknown metric → exit 2 ✓
  - Scenario 7: Markdown report with thresholds ✓
  - Scenario 8: Metric with no score → fails ✓
  - Scenario 9: No thresholds (backwards compat) ✓
  - Scenario 10: SDK usage ✓

  - TypeScript definitions for threshold-related functions
  - Ensure IDE autocomplete works for new parameters

  - Existing code without --threshold flag works unchanged
  - Existing SDK code calling generateReport without thresholds param works unchanged
  - Report format unchanged when thresholds not specified

  - Document validateThresholds, evaluateThresholds, formatThresholdError
  - Document generateReport threshold parameter
  - Include examples of usage
- [ ] T040 Final integration test: end-to-end CLI + SDK scenario
  - CLI: Run evaluation with threshold, verify exit code and report
  - SDK: Programmatically validate same data, verify results match
  - Both should produce identical threshold evaluations

**Checkpoint**: All user stories complete, tested, and validated; feature is production-ready

---

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies - verify existing packages
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup - provides core functions for all stories
- **User Story 1 (Phase 3, P1)**: Depends on Foundational - CLI feature
- **User Story 2 (Phase 4, P1)**: Depends on Foundational - SDK feature
- **User Story 3 (Phase 5, P2)**: Depends on US1 and US2 - report formatting
- **User Story 4 (Phase 6, P2)**: Depends on Foundational - error handling
- **User Story 5 (Phase 7, P2)**: Depends on Foundational - null handling
- **Polish (Phase 8)**: Depends on all user stories - comprehensive testing

### User Story Dependencies

- **US1 (CLI Gate)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - No dependencies on other stories
- **US2 (SDK Validation)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - Independent of CLI
- **US3 (Report Writing)**: Depends on US1 AND US2 both being mostly complete (report format)
- **US4 (Validation Errors)**: Depends on Foundational - error messages
- **US5 (Null Scores)**: Depends on Foundational - null handling

### Within Each Phase

- Tests → Implementation (each story's tests before implementation)
- Models → Services → Endpoints → Integration
- Validation before main logic

### Parallel Opportunities

- All Phase 2 tasks marked [P]: validation functions, helper functions can run in parallel
- US1 CLI tasks and US2 SDK tasks can run in parallel (both depend only on Phase 2)
- Within Phase 3 (US1): argument parsing and validation can be developed in parallel, then integrated
- Within Phase 4 (US2): generateReport modification and tests can run in parallel
- Within Phase 5 (US3): JSON and Markdown reporters can be modified in parallel
- Phase 2 must complete before US1/US2 start, but US1/US2 can proceed in parallel

---

## Parallel Example: User Story 1 & 2 (Both P1)

Once Foundational (Phase 2) is complete:

```
Developer A:
  T010: Modify CLI option parsing
  T011: Add CLI argument validation
  T012: Modify runEvalCommand for exit codes
  T013: Add CLI tests

Developer B:
  T014: Modify generateReport signature
  T015: Add threshold evaluation logic
  T016: Add SDK tests
  T017: Add integration test

Both run in parallel; only dependency is Phase 2 completion.
```

---

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP First (User Story 1 + 2)

1. Complete Phase 1: Setup
2. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (CRITICAL)
3. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1 (CLI)
4. Complete Phase 4: User Story 2 (SDK)
5. **STOP and VALIDATE**: Run quickstart scenarios 1-3, 9-10
6. Deploy if ready

### Incremental Delivery

1. Phase 1 + Phase 2 → Foundation ready
2. Add Phase 3 (US1) → CLI threshold gating works
3. Add Phase 4 (US2) → SDK validation works
4. Add Phase 5 (US3) → Reports enhanced
5. Add Phase 6 (US4) → Error handling complete
6. Add Phase 7 (US5) → Null score handling complete
7. Phase 8 → Polish and final testing

### Single Developer Path

1. Setup + Foundational (T001-T009)
2. US1 CLI (T010-T013)
3. US2 SDK (T014-T017)
4. US3 Reporting (T018-T022)
5. US4 Errors (T023-T027)
6. US5 Null Scores (T028-T031)
7. Polish (T032-T040)

---

## Task Summary

| Phase | Tasks | Purpose |
|-------|-------|---------|
| 1 Setup | T001-T002 | Verify packages, prep test data |
| 2 Foundational | T003-T009 | Core validation logic (BLOCKING) |
| 3 US1 (P1) | T010-T013 | CLI threshold gating |
| 4 US2 (P1) | T014-T017 | SDK validation |
| 5 US3 (P2) | T018-T022 | Report formatting |
| 6 US4 (P2) | T023-T027 | Error messages |
| 7 US5 (P2) | T028-T031 | Null score handling |
| 8 Polish | T032-T040 | Testing & validation |
| **Total** | **40 tasks** | Complete implementation |

---

## Notes

- [P] tasks = different files, no blocking dependencies on incomplete tasks
- All Phase 2 tasks must complete before user story work begins
- Each user story phase should be independently completable and testable
- Tests are listed alongside implementation (test-driven approach)
- Commit after each task or logical group
- Stop at any checkpoint to validate the feature independently
- Quickstart.md scenarios are acceptance tests for the feature

# Tasks: Eval Threshold Validation

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/001-eval-thresholds/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story to enable independent implementation and testing of each story.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependencies on incomplete tasks)
- **[Story]**: Which user story this task belongs to (e.g., US1, US2, US3, US4, US5)
- Include exact file paths in descriptions

---

## Phase 1: Setup (Existing Packages)

**Purpose**: Project already exists; this phase prepares for threshold feature addition

- [x] T001 Verify packages/frai-core and packages/frai-cli are built and dependencies resolved
- [x] T002 Create test data files for threshold validation scenarios in /tmp or test fixtures

---

## Phase 2: Foundational (Core Threshold Logic - Blocking All Stories)

**Purpose**: Core validation and helper functions that ALL user stories depend on

**⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story work can begin until this phase is complete

- [x] T003 [P] Create threshold validation function in packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js
  - Function: `validateThresholds(thresholds, registeredMetricIds)`
  - Validates format: `{ metric_id: number }`
  - Returns: `{ valid: boolean, errors: string[] }`
  - Must validate: metric IDs exist in registered metrics, values are 0.0–1.0 inclusive
- [x] T004 [P] Create threshold evaluation function in packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js
  - Function: `evaluateThresholds(thresholds, evaluations)`
  - Input: thresholds object, array of metric results
  - Output: array `[{ metric, min, score, passed }, ...]`
  - Rule: metric with null/undefined score → passed: false
  - Rule: comparison is `score >= min && score !== null`
- [x] T005 [P] Create helper to get all registered metric IDs in packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js
  - Function: `getRegisteredMetricIds()` → returns array of valid metric IDs
  - Include: exact_match, toxicity, length_variance
  - Must support custom metrics from DEFAULT_METRICS
- [x] T006 Create threshold error message formatter in packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js
  - Function: `formatThresholdError(type, value, validIds)`
  - Types: format_error, range_error, unknown_metric
  - Return user-friendly error strings with valid metric list for unknown_metric errors
- [x] T007 [P] Add tests for validateThresholds in packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js
  - Test format validation (missing =, invalid format)
  - Test range validation (< 0.0, > 1.0)
  - Test valid thresholds pass
- [x] T008 [P] Add tests for evaluateThresholds in packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js
  - Test metric with score passes/fails correctly
  - Test metric with null score always fails
  - Test multiple thresholds, mixed pass/fail
  - Test custom metrics work
- [x] T009 Add tests for getRegisteredMetricIds in packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.test.js
  - Verify list includes exact_match, toxicity, length_variance
  - Verify custom metrics can be included

**Checkpoint**: Foundation ready - all validation logic is tested and working ✓

---

## Phase 3: User Story 1 - CI Pipeline Quality Gate (Priority: P1) 🎯 MVP

**Goal**: Enable CLI to gate CI jobs on metric thresholds with proper exit codes

**Independent Test**: Run `frai eval --threshold exact_match=0.9` on sample data; verify exit code 0 when score ≥ 0.9, exit code 1 when score < 0.9

### Implementation for User Story 1

- [x] T010 Modify CLI option parsing in packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts
  - Add `--threshold <metric>=<min>` option to eval command (repeatable)
  - Parse each threshold into object form `{ [metric]: number }`
  - Accumulate multiple thresholds (last one wins for duplicate metrics)
- [x] T011 Add CLI argument validation in packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts (runEvalCommand)
  - Call validateThresholds before running evaluation
  - Exit 2 with error message if validation fails
  - Do NOT call generateReport on validation error
  - Error messages must list valid metric IDs for unknown_metric errors
- [x] T012 Modify runEvalCommand in packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts
  - Pass thresholds to Eval.generateReport() call
  - Set exit code based on report.passed field
  - Exit 0 if no thresholds specified (backwards compatibility)
  - Exit 0 if all thresholds passed
  - Exit 1 if any threshold failed
  - Exit 2 if validation error (already handled)
- [x] T013 Add CLI tests in packages/frai-cli/src/index.test.ts
  - Test: `frai eval --threshold exact_match=0.9` with passing score → exit 0
  - Test: `frai eval --threshold exact_match=0.9` with failing score → exit 1
  - Test: `frai eval --threshold exact_match=0.9` with null score → exit 1
  - Test: Multiple thresholds, one fails → exit 1
  - Test: No threshold flag → exit 0 (backwards compat)

**Checkpoint**: CLI accepts --threshold flag, validates arguments, and exits with correct codes ✓

---

## Phase 4: User Story 2 - SDK Programmatic Validation (Priority: P1)

**Goal**: SDK users can validate thresholds via generateReport() function

**Independent Test**: Call `Eval.generateReport({ evaluations, thresholds: { exact_match: 0.9 } })` and verify report includes `passed` field and `thresholds` array

### Implementation for User Story 2

- [x] T014 Modify generateReport signature in packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js
  - Add optional parameter: `thresholds` (object with metric IDs as keys)
  - If thresholds provided: validate (throw on unknown metric)
  - If thresholds provided: evaluate and add to report
  - If thresholds NOT provided: skip (backwards compatible, no new fields)
- [x] T015 Add threshold evaluation logic in packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js (generateReport)
  - Call evaluateThresholds(thresholds, evaluations)
  - Add `passed: boolean` field (true if all thresholds passed)
  - Add `thresholds: array` field with threshold results
  - Only add these fields if thresholds parameter was provided

  - Test: generateReport with thresholds → includes passed and thresholds fields
  - Test: All thresholds pass → passed: true

# Tasks: Eval Threshold Validation

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/001-eval-thresholds/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story to enable independent implementation and testing of each story.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependencies on incomplete tasks)
- **[Story]**: Which user story this task belongs to (e.g., US1, US2, US3, US4, US5)
- Include exact file paths in descriptions

---

## Phase 1: Setup (Existing Packages)

**Purpose**: Project already exists; this phase prepares for threshold feature addition

- [x] T001 Verify packages/frai-core and packages/frai-cli are built and dependencies resolved
- [x] T002 Create test data files for threshold validation scenarios in /tmp or test fixtures

---

## Phase 2: Foundational (Core Threshold Logic - Blocking All Stories)

**Purpose**: Core validation and helper functions that ALL user stories depend on

**⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story work can begin until this phase is complete

- [x] T003 [P] Create threshold validation function in packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js
  - Function: `validateThresholds(thresholds, registeredMetricIds)`
  - Validates format: `{ metric_id: number }`
  - Returns: `{ valid: boolean, errors: string[] }`
  - Must validate: metric IDs exist in registered metrics, values are 0.0–1.0 inclusive
- [x] T004 [P] Create threshold evaluation function in packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js
  - Function: `evaluateThresholds(thresholds, evaluations)`
  - Input: thresholds object, array of metric results
  - Output: array `[{ metric, min, score, passed }, ...]`
  - Rule: metric with null/undefined score → passed: false
  - Rule: comparison is `score >= min && score !== null`
- [x] T005 [P] Create helper to get all registered metric IDs in packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js
  - Function: `getRegisteredMetricIds()` → returns array of valid metric IDs
  - Include: exact_match, toxicity, length_variance
  - Must support custom metrics from DEFAULT_METRICS
- [x] T006 Create threshold error message formatter in packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js
  - Function: `formatThresholdError(type, value, validIds)`
  - Types: format_error, range_error, unknown_metric
  - Return user-friendly error strings with valid metric list for unknown_metric errors
- [x] T007 [P] Add tests for validateThresholds in packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js
  - Test format validation (missing =, invalid format)
  - Test range validation (< 0.0, > 1.0)
  - Test valid thresholds pass
- [x] T008 [P] Add tests for evaluateThresholds in packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js
  - Test metric with score passes/fails correctly
  - Test metric with null score always fails
  - Test multiple thresholds, mixed pass/fail
  - Test custom metrics work
- [x] T009 Add tests for getRegisteredMetricIds in packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.test.js
  - Verify list includes exact_match, toxicity, length_variance
  - Verify custom metrics can be included

**Checkpoint**: Foundation ready - all validation logic is tested and working ✓

---

## Phase 3: User Story 1 - CI Pipeline Quality Gate (Priority: P1) 🎯 MVP

**Goal**: Enable CLI to gate CI jobs on metric thresholds with proper exit codes

**Independent Test**: Run `frai eval --threshold exact_match=0.9` on sample data; verify exit code 0 when score ≥ 0.9, exit code 1 when score < 0.9

### Implementation for User Story 1

- [x] T010 Modify CLI option parsing in packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts
  - Add `--threshold <metric>=<min>` option to eval command (repeatable)
  - Parse each threshold into object form `{ [metric]: number }`
  - Accumulate multiple thresholds (last one wins for duplicate metrics)
- [x] T011 Add CLI argument validation in packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts (runEvalCommand)

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup - provides core functions for all stories
- **User Story 1 (Phase 3, P1)**: Depends on Foundational - CLI feature
- **User Story 2 (Phase 4, P1)**: Depends on Foundational - SDK feature
- **User Story 3 (Phase 5, P2)**: Depends on US1 and US2 - report formatting
- **User Story 4 (Phase 6, P2)**: Depends on Foundational - error handling
- **User Story 5 (Phase 7, P2)**: Depends on Foundational - null handling
- **Polish (Phase 8)**: Depends on all user stories - comprehensive testing

### User Story Dependencies

- **US1 (CLI Gate)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - No dependencies on other stories
- **US2 (SDK Validation)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - Independent of CLI

- **US5 (Null Scores)**: Depends on Foundational - null handling

- Tests → Implementation (each story's tests before implementation)
- Models → Services → Endpoints → Integration
- Validation before main logic

- All Phase 2 tasks marked [P]: validation functions, helper functions can run in parallel
- US1 CLI tasks and US2 SDK tasks can run in parallel (both depend only on Phase 2)
- Within Phase 3 (US1): argument parsing and validation can be developed in parallel, then integrated
- Within Phase 4 (US2): generateReport modification and tests can run in parallel
- Within Phase 5 (US3): JSON and Markdown reporters can be modified in parallel
- Phase 2 must complete before US1/US2 start, but US1/US2 can proceed in parallel
